question: Will US CPI inflation for November 2026 be 4.0% or higher year on year?
resolution_criteria: Yes if FRED CPIAUCSL (seasonally adjusted) for 2026-11-01 divided by the value for 2025-11-01 (325.063 as of 2026-11-17) minus 1 is >= 0.040, using the first value FRED publishes for November 2026.

reasoning.outside_view: Needs month-on-month growth of at least 0.175% from October's 337.476. The last 12 monthly changes average 0.338% (sd 0.313%): 0.70 on a normal model; 18 of the last 24 months cleared 0.175% (0.75).
reasoning.decomposition: One monthly print against a fixed bar; YoY was 3.72% in September 2026.
reasoning.inside_view: Rate hikes act with long lags and the recent prints (0.40, 0.65, 0.35) are above the bar; energy can swing a single month either way. October 2025 has no CPI observation on FRED, so the series has a recent gap worth watching for revisions.
reasoning.what_would_change_my_mind: A large energy-price drop in November, or a soft October core print, moves this toward 0.5.
